title: Management Accounting
topics: Nature and scope of management accounting

items.q: A firm has current assets of N620000 and current liabilities of N380000. What is its working capital?
items.s: Working capital = current assets - current liabilities = 620000 - 380000 = 240000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 18000 units, opening finished stock is 1500 units and closing finished stock is 1800 units. What is the production budget?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 18000 + 1800 - 1500 = 18300 units.

items.q: The production budget is 4000 units. Each unit needs 3 hours at a wage rate of N100 an hour. What is the direct labour budget?
items.s: Labour budget = 4000 x 3 x 100 = 1200000 naira.

items.q: A project costs N800000 and yields N260000 a year for 5 years with no discounting. What is the total surplus before any allowance for the cost of waiting?
items.s: Total inflow = 260000 x 5 = 1300000; surplus over cost = 1300000 - 800000 = 500000 naira.

items.q: The full cost of a component is N130 and the transfer price is set at cost plus 10 percent. What is the transfer price?
items.s: Transfer price = 130 x (100 + 10)/100 = 143 naira.

items.q: Profit after tax is N900000 and there are 900000 ordinary shares in issue. What is the earnings per share in naira?
items.s: Earnings per share = profit after tax/number of shares = 900000/900000 = 1 naira.

items.q: In the busiest month a firm made 12000 units at a total cost of N400000. In the quietest month it made 4000 units at a total cost of N160000. Using the high and low method, what is the variable cost per unit?
items.s: Variable cost per unit = change in cost/change in units = (400000 - 160000)/(12000 - 4000) = 30 naira.

items.q: Total cost was N160000 at an output of 2000 units and N460000 at an output of 12000 units. Using the high and low method, what is the fixed cost for the period?
Supervision costs N60000 for every 3000 units of output or part of that number. Material costs N15 a unit. What is the total of these two costs at an output of 5000 units?
items.s: The output needs 2 steps of supervision costing 2 x 60000 = 120000, so the total = 120000 + 15 x 5000 = 195000 naira.

items.q: Sales for the year were N1200000 and the cost of the goods sold was N500000. What is the gross profit margin as a percentage of sales?
items.s: Gross margin = (sales - cost of sales)/sales x 100 = (1200000 - 500000)/1200000 x 100 = 58.33 percent.

items.q: Operating profit for the year was N600000 and the capital employed was N5000000. What is the return on capital employed, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on capital employed = operating profit/capital employed x 100 = 600000/5000000 x 100 = 12 percent.

items.q: Trading profit before interest is N1800000 and the interest charge for the year is N200000. What is the interest cover, in times?
items.s: Interest cover = profit before interest/interest = 1800000/200000 = 9 times.

items.q: A firm has long term debt of N1200000 and shareholders' funds of N2400000. What is the gearing ratio, debt as a percentage of total long term funds?
items.s: Gearing = debt/(debt + equity) x 100 = 1200000/(1200000 + 2400000) x 100 = 33.33 percent.

items.q: Stock is held on average for 45 days, customers take 50 days to pay and the firm takes 35 days to pay its suppliers. What is the length of the cash operating cycle in days?
items.s: Cash cycle = stock days + receivable days - payable days = 45 + 50 - 35 = 60 days.

items.q: Annual demand for a material is 7200 units. The cost of placing one order is N125 and the cost of holding one unit for a year is N20. What is the economic order quantity in units?
items.s: Economic order quantity = square root of (2 x annual demand x order cost/holding cost) = square root of (2 x 7200 x 125/20) = square root of 90000 = 300 units.

items.q: The cash budget opens with a balance of N240000. Receipts are expected to be N2100000 and payments N1650000. What closing cash balance is budgeted?
items.s: Closing balance = opening + receipts - payments = 240000 + 2100000 - 1650000 = 690000 naira.

items.q: The production budget is 8000 units and each unit needs 3 kilograms of a material. Opening stock of the material is 1000 kilograms and closing stock is 1200 kilograms. What is the material purchase budget in kilograms?
At a budgeted output of 4000 units the variable cost is N25 a unit and the fixed cost is N200000. What cost should be allowed if 4200 units are actually produced?
items.s: Allowed cost = 25 x 4200 + 200000 = 305000 naira.

items.q: The budget allowed spending of N900000 for the period and the actual spending was N800000. What is the variance, taking an underspend as positive and an overspend as negative?
items.s: Variance = allowed - actual = 900000 - 800000 = 100000 naira.

items.q: A part can be made in house for variable cost of N260000 or bought outside for N360000. Fixed overhead of N140000 is unaffected either way. What is the saving from making rather than buying?
items.s: Saving = purchase price - variable cost of making = 360000 - 260000 = 100000 naira; the fixed overhead does not change.

items.q: A customer offers to buy 3000 units at N55 each. The variable cost is N38 a unit and there is spare capacity, so no fixed cost changes. What extra contribution does the order bring?
items.s: Extra contribution = (price - variable cost) x units = (55 - 38) x 3000 = 51000 naira.

items.q: A product line sells for N1500000, its variable cost is N900000 and the fixed cost that would disappear if the line were dropped is N200000. What is the segment margin?
items.s: Segment margin = sales - variable cost - avoidable fixed cost = 1500000 - 900000 - 200000 = 400000 naira.

items.q: A product earns a contribution of N80 a unit and each unit needs 4 kilograms of a scarce material. What is the contribution per kilogram of the scarce material?
items.s: Contribution per kilogram = 80/4 = 20 naira.

items.q: A machine costs N1500000 and is expected to earn an average annual profit of N160000 over its life. What is the accounting rate of return on the initial investment, as a percentage?
items.s: Accounting rate of return = average profit/initial investment x 100 = 160000/1500000 x 100 = 10.67 percent.

items.q: A project costs N1000000 now and brings in N700000 after one year and N700000 after two years. The discount factors are 0.901 at year one and 0.826 at year two. What is the net present value?
A project has a present value of future returns of N900000 and an initial cost of N600000. What is its profitability index?
items.s: Profitability index = present value of returns/initial cost = 900000/600000 = 1.5.

items.q: A project is expected to bring in N1500000 in four years from now. The discount factor for year four is 0.564. What is the present value of that inflow?
items.s: Present value = cash flow x discount factor = 1500000 x 0.564 = 846000 naira.

items.q: A division earns a profit of N760000 on assets of N3200000, and the firm charges 12 percent for the funds employed. What is the residual income?
A division made a profit of N540000 on assets employed of N2700000. What return on investment did it earn, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on investment = 540000/2700000 x 100 = 20 percent.

items.q: A manager's unit has sales of N800000, variable cost of N420000 and fixed cost under his control of N200000. What is the controllable margin?
items.s: Controllable margin = sales - variable cost - controllable fixed cost = 800000 - 420000 - 200000 = 180000 naira.

items.q: A share currently sells for N180. The dividend just paid was N24 and dividends are expected to grow at 8 percent a year. Using the dividend growth model, what is the cost of equity as a percentage?
items.s: Next dividend = 24 x (100 + 8)/100 = 25.92; cost of equity = 25.92/180 x 100 + 8 = 22.4 percent.

items.q: A firm has equity of N6000000 costing 12 percent and debt of N2000000 costing 9 percent. Ignoring tax, what is the weighted average cost of capital as a percentage?
items.s: Weighted average = (6000000 x 12 + 2000000 x 9)/8000000 = 11.25 percent.

items.q: A firm borrows at 15 percent and pays tax at 40 percent. What is the after tax cost of debt as a percentage?
items.s: After tax cost of debt = rate x (100 - tax)/100 = 15 x (100 - 40)/100 = 9 percent.

items.q: A company earned a profit after tax of N600000 and paid an ordinary dividend of N240000. What is the dividend payout ratio as a percentage?
items.s: Payout ratio = dividend/profit after tax x 100 = 240000/600000 x 100 = 40 percent.

items.q: A department has a fixed cost of N120000 for the period and a variable cost of N35 a unit. It produced 6000 units. What is the total cost?
items.s: Total cost = fixed + variable x units = 120000 + 35 x 6000 = 330000 naira.

items.q: A firm has current assets of N950000 and current liabilities of N450000. What is its working capital?
items.s: Working capital = current assets - current liabilities = 950000 - 450000 = 500000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 9000 units, opening finished stock is 800 units and closing finished stock is 1200 units. What is the production budget?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 9000 + 1200 - 800 = 9400 units.

items.q: The production budget is 6000 units. Each unit needs 3 hours at a wage rate of N150 an hour. What is the direct labour budget?
items.s: Labour budget = 6000 x 3 x 150 = 2700000 naira.

items.q: A project costs N1000000 and yields N300000 a year for 6 years with no discounting. What is the total surplus before any allowance for the cost of waiting?
items.s: Total inflow = 300000 x 6 = 1800000; surplus over cost = 1800000 - 1000000 = 800000 naira.

items.q: In the busiest month a firm made 8000 units at a total cost of N240000. In the quietest month it made 3000 units at a total cost of N115000. Using the high and low method, what is the variable cost per unit?
items.s: Variable cost per unit = change in cost/change in units = (240000 - 115000)/(8000 - 3000) = 25 naira.

items.q: Total cost was N80000 at an output of 2000 units and N240000 at an output of 10000 units. Using the high and low method, what is the fixed cost for the period?
Supervision costs N50000 for every 2500 units of output or part of that number. Material costs N12 a unit. What is the total of these two costs at an output of 6000 units?
items.s: The output needs 3 steps of supervision costing 3 x 50000 = 150000, so the total = 150000 + 12 x 6000 = 222000 naira.

items.q: Sales for the year were N800000 and the cost of the goods sold was N750000. What is the gross profit margin as a percentage of sales?
items.s: Gross margin = (sales - cost of sales)/sales x 100 = (800000 - 750000)/800000 x 100 = 6.25 percent.

items.q: Operating profit for the year was N360000 and the capital employed was N4000000. What is the return on capital employed, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on capital employed = operating profit/capital employed x 100 = 360000/4000000 x 100 = 9 percent.

items.q: A firm has long term debt of N1500000 and shareholders' funds of N2400000. What is the gearing ratio, debt as a percentage of total long term funds?
items.s: Gearing = debt/(debt + equity) x 100 = 1500000/(1500000 + 2400000) x 100 = 38.46 percent.

items.q: Cost of the goods sold for the year was N1500000 and the average stock held was N150000. How many times did stock turn over in the year?
items.s: Stock turnover = cost of goods sold/average stock = 1500000/150000 = 10 times.

items.q: Stock is held on average for 90 days, customers take 50 days to pay and the firm takes 20 days to pay its suppliers. What is the length of the cash operating cycle in days?
items.s: Cash cycle = stock days + receivable days - payable days = 90 + 50 - 20 = 120 days.

items.q: Annual demand for a material is 14400 units. The cost of placing one order is N100 and the cost of holding one unit for a year is N8. What is the economic order quantity in units?
items.s: Economic order quantity = square root of (2 x annual demand x order cost/holding cost) = square root of (2 x 14400 x 100/8) = square root of 360000 = 600 units.

items.q: The cash budget opens with a balance of N180000. Receipts are expected to be N1500000 and payments N1400000. What closing cash balance is budgeted?
items.s: Closing balance = opening + receipts - payments = 180000 + 1500000 - 1400000 = 280000 naira.

items.q: The production budget is 4000 units and each unit needs 3 kilograms of a material. Opening stock of the material is 2000 kilograms and closing stock is 1200 kilograms. What is the material purchase budget in kilograms?
At a budgeted output of 4000 units the variable cost is N55 a unit and the fixed cost is N200000. What cost should be allowed if 5000 units are actually produced?
items.s: Allowed cost = 55 x 5000 + 200000 = 475000 naira.

items.q: The budget allowed spending of N900000 for the period and the actual spending was N640000. What is the variance, taking an underspend as positive and an overspend as negative?
items.s: Variance = allowed - actual = 900000 - 640000 = 260000 naira.

items.q: A part can be made in house for variable cost of N180000 or bought outside for N300000. Fixed overhead of N80000 is unaffected either way. What is the saving from making rather than buying?
items.s: Saving = purchase price - variable cost of making = 300000 - 180000 = 120000 naira; the fixed overhead does not change.

items.q: A customer offers to buy 4000 units at N50 each. The variable cost is N34 a unit and there is spare capacity, so no fixed cost changes. What extra contribution does the order bring?
items.s: Extra contribution = (price - variable cost) x units = (50 - 34) x 4000 = 64000 naira.

items.q: A product line sells for N1500000, its variable cost is N700000 and the fixed cost that would disappear if the line were dropped is N200000. What is the segment margin?
items.s: Segment margin = sales - variable cost - avoidable fixed cost = 1500000 - 700000 - 200000 = 600000 naira.

items.q: A product earns a contribution of N80 a unit and each unit needs 5 kilograms of a scarce material. What is the contribution per kilogram of the scarce material?
items.s: Contribution per kilogram = 80/5 = 16 naira.

items.q: A division earns a contribution of N300000 but carries fixed costs of N320000 that would be saved if it were closed. How much better off is the firm if the division is closed?
items.s: Closing saves fixed cost 320000 but loses contribution 300000, so the gain is 320000 - 300000 = 20000 naira.

items.q: A machine costs N1200000 and is expected to earn an average annual profit of N200000 over its life. What is the accounting rate of return on the initial investment, as a percentage?
items.s: Accounting rate of return = average profit/initial investment x 100 = 200000/1200000 x 100 = 16.67 percent.

items.q: A project costs N1500000 now and brings in N700000 after one year and N700000 after two years. The discount factors are 0.901 at year one and 0.797 at year two. What is the net present value?
A project has a present value of future returns of N1000000 and an initial cost of N800000. What is its profitability index?
items.s: Profitability index = present value of returns/initial cost = 1000000/800000 = 1.25.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines step cost?
o: a charge that holds steady over a range of activity and then jumps to a new level
the number of times trading profit can meet the yearly charge on borrowed money
outlay that stays the same in total whatever the level of activity within the period
the resource in shortest supply that caps the level of activity
items.s: step cost: a charge that holds steady over a range of activity and then jumps to a new level. The other options describe limiting factor, fixed cost, interest cover.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines collection period?
o: the state in which what is best for a unit is also best for the whole firm
the part of the money summary that deals with buying and selling long lived assets
the money a project is worth today after allowing for the cost of waiting
the average number of days taken by customers to settle what they owe
items.s: collection period: the average number of days taken by customers to settle what they owe. The other options describe goal congruence, investing activities, net present value.

items.q: dividend payout ratio may be defined as
o: valuing a share from the payout just made, its expected rise and the return required
the return the suppliers of funds must be offered to part with their money
the part of the profit of the year handed to the ordinary shareholders
the surplus a unit of the firm makes after charging the items it controls
items.s: dividend payout ratio: the part of the profit of the year handed to the ordinary shareholders. The other options describe dividend growth model, divisional profit, cost of capital.

items.q: Which of the following best describes operating activities?
o: the average number of days taken by customers to settle what they owe
the part of the money summary that comes from the ordinary trading of the firm
a part of the firm whose manager is held answerable for a stated set of figures
outlay that carries on whether or not a particular activity continues
items.s: operating activities: the part of the money summary that comes from the ordinary trading of the firm. The other options describe unavoidable cost, collection period, responsibility centre.

items.q: Which term is described by “outlay that the manager of a unit is able to influence by his own decisions”?
o: cost centre
management accounting
management by exception
controllable cost
items.s: controllable cost is outlay that the manager of a unit is able to influence by his own decisions.
items.t: Nature and scope of management accounting

items.q: Which of the following best describes semi-variable cost?
o: what a manager earns on the items his own decisions can change
sales value divided by the total resources used to earn it
outlay made up of a standing part and a part that moves with activity
a part of the firm whose manager is held answerable for a stated set of figures
items.s: semi-variable cost: outlay made up of a standing part and a part that moves with activity. The other options describe controllable margin, asset turnover, responsibility centre.

items.q: Which of the following best describes residual value?
o: the amount by which a future sum is scaled down to state it in today's terms
what a project or asset is expected to fetch at the close of its useful life
a charge that holds steady over a range of activity and then jumps to a new level
the surplus a unit of the firm makes after charging the items it controls
items.s: residual value: what a project or asset is expected to fetch at the close of its useful life. The other options describe discount factor, divisional profit, step cost.

items.q: responsibility centre may be defined as
o: a plan kept the same length by adding a further period each time one expires
a set of measures covering money, customers, internal work and learning
a part of the firm whose manager is held answerable for a stated set of figures
sales value less the cost of the materials used in the items sold
items.s: responsibility centre: a part of the firm whose manager is held answerable for a stated set of figures. The other options describe throughput contribution, rolling budget, balanced scorecard.
items.t: Nature and scope of management accounting

items.q: Which of the following best describes relevant range?
o: the band of activity within which the assumed pattern of behaviour holds good
a short lived investment that can be turned into money at once with little risk
the surplus a unit of the firm makes after charging the items it controls
the rise or fall in the excess of current resources over short obligations
items.s: relevant range: the band of activity within which the assumed pattern of behaviour holds good. The other options describe working capital movement, cash equivalent, divisional profit.

items.q: Which term is described by “a set of measures covering money, customers, internal work and learning”?
o: divisional profit
balanced scorecard
segment margin
controllable margin
items.s: balanced scorecard is a set of measures covering money, customers, internal work and learning.

items.q: All of the following belong to Cost classification and behaviour EXCEPT
o: fixed cost
economic value added
variable cost
semi-variable cost
items.s: Every other option belongs to Cost classification and behaviour. “economic value added” belongs to Divisional performance measurement, not Cost classification and behaviour.

items.q: The statement “building every figure afresh so each item must be justified from nothing” describes which of the following?
o: incremental budgeting
zero-based budgeting
cash budget
flexible budget
items.s: zero-based budgeting is building every figure afresh so each item must be justified from nothing.

items.q: The statement “outlay that would cease if a particular activity were dropped” describes which of the following?
o: avoidable cost
make or buy decision
limiting factor
unavoidable cost
items.s: avoidable cost is outlay that would cease if a particular activity were dropped.

items.q: Which of the following best describes cost of equity?
o: the number of times the average holding is sold in the course of a year
the worth of the best choice given up in order to take another
the return that holders of ordinary shares expect on their stake
what a project or asset is expected to fetch at the close of its useful life
items.s: cost of equity: the return that holders of ordinary shares expect on their stake. The other options describe opportunity cost, inventory turnover, residual value.

items.q: Which term is described by “an amount deducted from profit that involves no money leaving the firm”?
o: operating activities
investing activities
non-cash charge
working capital movement
items.s: non-cash charge is an amount deducted from profit that involves no money leaving the firm.

items.q: The statement “a summary of the money that moved in and out of the firm during a period” describes which of the following?
o: cash flow statement
financing activities
funds flow
operating activities
items.s: cash flow statement is a summary of the money that moved in and out of the firm during a period.

items.q: Which of the following best describes high and low method?
o: working out the variable part per unit from the difference between the busiest and quietest periods
outlay that would cease if a particular activity were dropped
the rise or fall in the excess of current resources over short obligations
the cushion a manager builds into his plan to make the target easier to beat
items.s: high and low method: working out the variable part per unit from the difference between the busiest and quietest periods. The other options describe budget slack, avoidable cost, working capital movement.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines high and low method?
o: sales value less the cost of the materials used in the items sold
working out the variable part per unit from the difference between the busiest and quietest periods
a position in which a firm grows faster than the funds it has to support the growth
the effective rate a firm pays on borrowed money once tax relief is allowed for
items.s: high and low method: working out the variable part per unit from the difference between the busiest and quietest periods. The other options describe overtrading, throughput contribution, cost of debt.

items.q: interest cover may be defined as
o: an amount deducted from profit that involves no money leaving the firm
a limit on the funds available for projects, so that the best must be chosen
the movement of resources shown by comparing two balance sheets
the number of times trading profit can meet the yearly charge on borrowed money
items.s: interest cover: the number of times trading profit can meet the yearly charge on borrowed money. The other options describe capital rationing, non-cash charge, funds flow.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines special order?
o: a position in which a firm grows faster than the funds it has to support the growth
a charge that holds steady over a range of activity and then jumps to a new level
a one-off request to supply at a price below the normal one
the resource in shortest supply that caps the level of activity
items.s: special order: a one-off request to supply at a price below the normal one. The other options describe step cost, overtrading, limiting factor.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines controllable cost?
o: outlay that the manager of a unit is able to influence by his own decisions
the number of times trading profit can meet the yearly charge on borrowed money
the part of the money summary that comes from the ordinary trading of the firm
a future outlay that differs between the alternatives being weighed
items.s: controllable cost: outlay that the manager of a unit is able to influence by his own decisions. The other options describe operating activities, relevant cost, interest cover.
items.t: Nature and scope of management accounting

items.q: master budget may be defined as
o: sales value divided by the total resources used to earn it
the set of linked plans that together form the whole forecast for a period
the branch that reports the results of a firm to parties outside it
a plan kept the same length by adding a further period each time one expires
items.s: master budget: the set of linked plans that together form the whole forecast for a period. The other options describe asset turnover, financial accounting, rolling budget.

items.q: budget may be defined as
o: a quantified plan covering a stated stretch of time
the part of the profit of the year handed to the ordinary shareholders
a position in which a firm grows faster than the funds it has to support the growth
a charge that holds steady over a range of activity and then jumps to a new level
items.s: budget: a quantified plan covering a stated stretch of time. The other options describe step cost, overtrading, dividend payout ratio.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines incremental budgeting?
o: the resource in shortest supply that caps the level of activity
the number of times the average holding is sold in the course of a year
building next period on the figures of this one with a margin added
a position in which a firm grows faster than the funds it has to support the growth
items.s: incremental budgeting: building next period on the figures of this one with a margin added. The other options describe limiting factor, inventory turnover, overtrading.

items.q: The statement “the cushion a manager builds into his plan to make the target easier to beat” describes which of the following?
o: flexible budget
master budget
budget slack
incremental budgeting
items.s: budget slack is the cushion a manager builds into his plan to make the target easier to beat.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines controllable margin.
o: what a manager earns on the items his own decisions can change
what a part of the business earns after its own avoidable outlay is charged
the share of long term funds that carries a fixed return
a future outlay that differs between the alternatives being weighed
items.s: controllable margin: what a manager earns on the items his own decisions can change. The other options describe relevant cost, segment margin, gearing ratio.

items.q: Which term is described by “the resource in shortest supply that caps the level of activity”?
o: relevant cost
limiting factor
make or buy decision
throughput contribution
items.s: limiting factor is the resource in shortest supply that caps the level of activity.

items.q: collection period may be defined as
o: the blended return required, each source counted in proportion to its share of the total
a part of the firm answerable for profit and also for the assets it employs
a position in which a firm grows faster than the funds it has to support the growth
the average number of days taken by customers to settle what they owe
items.s: collection period: the average number of days taken by customers to settle what they owe. The other options describe overtrading, weighted average cost of capital, investment centre.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines zero-based budgeting.
o: the state in which what is best for a unit is also best for the whole firm
the cushion a manager builds into his plan to make the target easier to beat
outlay that moves in direct proportion to the number of items produced
building every figure afresh so each item must be justified from nothing
items.s: zero-based budgeting: building every figure afresh so each item must be justified from nothing. The other options describe goal congruence, budget slack, variable cost.

items.q: The statement “the practice of acting only on the differences that are large enough to matter” describes which of the following?
o: management by exception
controllable cost
profit centre
management accounting
items.s: management by exception is the practice of acting only on the differences that are large enough to matter.
items.t: Nature and scope of management accounting

items.q: Which term is described by “the excess of current resources over the obligations falling due within a year”?
o: economic order quantity
inventory turnover
payment period
working capital
items.s: working capital is the excess of current resources over the obligations falling due within a year.

items.q: residual income may be defined as
o: profit left after deducting a charge for the resources a unit employs
the resource in shortest supply that caps the level of activity
a future outlay that differs between the alternatives being weighed
a plan kept the same length by adding a further period each time one expires
items.s: residual income: profit left after deducting a charge for the resources a unit employs. The other options describe relevant cost, rolling budget, limiting factor.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines inventory turnover.
o: a one-off request to supply at a price below the normal one
a summary of the money that moved in and out of the firm during a period
the number of times the average holding is sold in the course of a year
the band of activity within which the assumed pattern of behaviour holds good
items.s: inventory turnover: the number of times the average holding is sold in the course of a year. The other options describe cash flow statement, relevant range, special order.

items.q: Which of the following best describes master budget?
o: a part of the firm whose manager is held answerable for a stated set of figures
the band of activity within which the assumed pattern of behaviour holds good
a position in which a firm grows faster than the funds it has to support the growth
the set of linked plans that together form the whole forecast for a period
items.s: master budget: the set of linked plans that together form the whole forecast for a period. The other options describe overtrading, relevant range, responsibility centre.

items.q: Which of the following best describes budget?
o: valuing a share from the payout just made, its expected rise and the return required
the stretch of time from paying for stock to collecting the cash from its sale
what a manager earns on the items his own decisions can change
a quantified plan covering a stated stretch of time
items.s: budget: a quantified plan covering a stated stretch of time. The other options describe dividend growth model, controllable margin, operating cycle.

items.q: asset turnover may be defined as
o: the branch that prepares figures for managers inside the firm to plan and decide with
valuing a share from the payout just made, its expected rise and the return required
the stretch of time from paying for stock to collecting the cash from its sale
sales value divided by the total resources used to earn it
items.s: asset turnover: sales value divided by the total resources used to earn it. The other options describe dividend growth model, management accounting, operating cycle.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines cost of debt?
o: a short lived investment that can be turned into money at once with little risk
the blended return required, each source counted in proportion to its share of the total
the effective rate a firm pays on borrowed money once tax relief is allowed for
the return the suppliers of funds must be offered to part with their money
items.s: cost of debt: the effective rate a firm pays on borrowed money once tax relief is allowed for. The other options describe cash equivalent, cost of capital, weighted average cost of capital.

items.q: Which term is described by “valuing a share from the payout just made, its expected rise and the return required”?
o: dividend payout ratio
dividend growth model
weighted average cost of capital
cost of debt
items.s: dividend growth model is valuing a share from the payout just made, its expected rise and the return required.

items.q: Which term is described by “the present worth of the returns divided by the sum first laid out”?
o: profitability index
residual value
payback period
accounting rate of return
items.s: profitability index is the present worth of the returns divided by the sum first laid out.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines asset turnover.
o: the number of times the average holding is sold in the course of a year
sales value divided by the total resources used to earn it
the excess of current resources over the obligations falling due within a year
what a manager earns on the items his own decisions can change
items.s: asset turnover: sales value divided by the total resources used to earn it. The other options describe working capital, controllable margin, inventory turnover.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines net present value.
o: building next period on the figures of this one with a margin added
sales value divided by the total resources used to earn it
the money a project is worth today after allowing for the cost of waiting
outlay that carries on whether or not a particular activity continues
items.s: net present value: the money a project is worth today after allowing for the cost of waiting. The other options describe unavoidable cost, asset turnover, incremental budgeting.

items.q: economic value added may be defined as
o: profit after a charge for the whole cost of the funds employed
the present worth of the returns divided by the sum first laid out
average yearly profit from a project shown as a percentage of the sum invested
outlay that would cease if a particular activity were dropped
items.s: economic value added: profit after a charge for the whole cost of the funds employed. The other options describe profitability index, accounting rate of return, avoidable cost.

items.q: All of the following belong to Budgeting and control EXCEPT
o: cash budget
segment margin
budget
master budget
items.s: Every other option belongs to Budgeting and control. “segment margin” belongs to Divisional performance measurement, not Budgeting and control.

items.q: special order may be defined as
o: outlay made up of a standing part and a part that moves with activity
a one-off request to supply at a price below the normal one
outlay that would cease if a particular activity were dropped
operating profit shown as a percentage of the long term funds invested
items.s: special order: a one-off request to supply at a price below the normal one. The other options describe avoidable cost, return on capital employed, semi-variable cost.

items.q: Which term is described by “the blended return required, each source counted in proportion to its share of the total”?
o: cost of capital
dividend payout ratio
weighted average cost of capital
cost of equity
items.s: weighted average cost of capital is the blended return required, each source counted in proportion to its share of the total.

items.q: Which term is described by “the part of the money summary that deals with buying and selling long lived assets”?
o: cash equivalent
non-cash charge
investing activities
working capital movement
items.s: investing activities is the part of the money summary that deals with buying and selling long lived assets.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines limiting factor?
o: the resource in shortest supply that caps the level of activity
the extra danger to shareholders that arises from borrowing
a part of the firm whose manager is held answerable for a stated set of figures
outlay that stays the same in total whatever the level of activity within the period
items.s: limiting factor: the resource in shortest supply that caps the level of activity. The other options describe fixed cost, responsibility centre, financial risk.

items.q: The statement “a charge that holds steady over a range of activity and then jumps to a new level” describes which of the following?
o: step cost
fixed cost
semi-variable cost
sunk cost
items.s: step cost is a charge that holds steady over a range of activity and then jumps to a new level.

items.q: Which of the following best describes flexible budget?
o: the amount by which a future sum is scaled down to state it in today's terms
a plan redrawn at the level of activity that was actually reached
the return the suppliers of funds must be offered to part with their money
the set of linked plans that together form the whole forecast for a period
items.s: flexible budget: a plan redrawn at the level of activity that was actually reached. The other options describe cost of capital, discount factor, master budget.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines relevant range.
o: the state in which what is best for a unit is also best for the whole firm
what a project or asset is expected to fetch at the close of its useful life
the band of activity within which the assumed pattern of behaviour holds good
the excess of current resources over the obligations falling due within a year
items.s: relevant range: the band of activity within which the assumed pattern of behaviour holds good. The other options describe working capital, residual value, goal congruence.

items.q: Which term is described by “outlay that carries on whether or not a particular activity continues”?
o: throughput contribution
unavoidable cost
make or buy decision
avoidable cost
items.s: unavoidable cost is outlay that carries on whether or not a particular activity continues.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines economic value added.
o: profit after a charge for the whole cost of the funds employed
profit kept inside the firm instead of being distributed
the average number of days taken by customers to settle what they owe
the number of times the average holding is sold in the course of a year
items.s: economic value added: profit after a charge for the whole cost of the funds employed. The other options describe collection period, retained earnings, inventory turnover.

items.q: Which term is described by “outlay that moves in direct proportion to the number of items produced”?
o: semi-variable cost
variable cost
step cost
opportunity cost
items.s: variable cost is outlay that moves in direct proportion to the number of items produced.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines relevant cost.
o: a position in which a firm grows faster than the funds it has to support the growth
a future outlay that differs between the alternatives being weighed
the part of the money summary that deals with buying and selling long lived assets
the part of the money summary that comes from the ordinary trading of the firm
items.s: relevant cost: a future outlay that differs between the alternatives being weighed. The other options describe investing activities, overtrading, operating activities.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines return on capital employed.

the part of the money summary that comes from the ordinary trading of the firm
outlay that would cease if a particular activity were dropped
operating profit shown as a percentage of the long term funds invested
items.s: return on capital employed: operating profit shown as a percentage of the long term funds invested. The other options describe payback period, avoidable cost, operating activities.

items.q: financial risk may be defined as
o: the length of time taken for the money coming back to equal the sum first laid out
outlay that moves in direct proportion to the number of items produced
what a project or asset is expected to fetch at the close of its useful life
the extra danger to shareholders that arises from borrowing
items.s: financial risk: the extra danger to shareholders that arises from borrowing. The other options describe residual value, payback period, variable cost.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines economic value added?
o: a short lived investment that can be turned into money at once with little risk
money spent already that no present choice can undo
profit after a charge for the whole cost of the funds employed
the length of time taken for the money coming back to equal the sum first laid out
items.s: economic value added: profit after a charge for the whole cost of the funds employed. The other options describe sunk cost, cash equivalent, payback period.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines collection period.
o: the worth of the best choice given up in order to take another
the average number of days taken by customers to settle what they owe
the effective rate a firm pays on borrowed money once tax relief is allowed for
a quantified plan covering a stated stretch of time
items.s: collection period: the average number of days taken by customers to settle what they owe. The other options describe opportunity cost, cost of debt, budget.

items.q: rolling budget may be defined as
o: the part of the money summary that comes from the ordinary trading of the firm
the average number of days the firm takes to settle what it owes suppliers
a plan kept the same length by adding a further period each time one expires
outlay that moves in direct proportion to the number of items produced
items.s: rolling budget: a plan kept the same length by adding a further period each time one expires. The other options describe operating activities, payment period, variable cost.

items.q: management by exception may be defined as
o: a summary of the money that moved in and out of the firm during a period
the practice of acting only on the differences that are large enough to matter
a future outlay that differs between the alternatives being weighed
a one-off request to supply at a price below the normal one
items.s: management by exception: the practice of acting only on the differences that are large enough to matter. The other options describe cash flow statement, relevant cost, special order.

items.q: Which term is described by “the number of times trading profit can meet the yearly charge on borrowed money”?
o: acid test ratio
interest cover
return on capital employed
ratio analysis
items.s: interest cover is the number of times trading profit can meet the yearly charge on borrowed money.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines net present value?
o: a short lived investment that can be turned into money at once with little risk
a one-off request to supply at a price below the normal one
a part of the firm whose manager is held answerable for a stated set of figures
the money a project is worth today after allowing for the cost of waiting

money spent already that no present choice can undo
outlay that stays the same in total whatever the level of activity within the period
the discount percentage at which a project is worth exactly nothing today

a one-off request to supply at a price below the normal one
a quantified plan covering a stated stretch of time
the amount one part of a firm charges another for goods or services
items.s: special order: a one-off request to supply at a price below the normal one. The other options describe budget, transfer price, discount factor.

items.q: Which term is described by “building every figure afresh so each item must be justified from nothing”?
o: zero-based budgeting
rolling budget
master budget
cash budget
items.s: zero-based budgeting is building every figure afresh so each item must be justified from nothing.

items.q: The cash budget opens with a balance of N300000. Receipts are expected to be N2100000 and payments N1400000. What closing cash balance is budgeted?
items.s: Closing balance = opening + receipts - payments = 300000 + 2100000 - 1400000 = 1000000 naira.

items.q: The production budget is 6000 units and each unit needs 4 kilograms of a material. Opening stock of the material is 1000 kilograms and closing stock is 1800 kilograms. What is the material purchase budget in kilograms?
A part can be made in house for variable cost of N260000 or bought outside for N300000. Fixed overhead of N80000 is unaffected either way. What is the saving from making rather than buying?
items.s: Saving = purchase price - variable cost of making = 300000 - 260000 = 40000 naira; the fixed overhead does not change.

items.q: A customer offers to buy 3000 units at N55 each. The variable cost is N34 a unit and there is spare capacity, so no fixed cost changes. What extra contribution does the order bring?
items.s: Extra contribution = (price - variable cost) x units = (55 - 34) x 3000 = 63000 naira.

items.q: A machine costs N1000000 and is expected to earn an average annual profit of N240000 over its life. What is the accounting rate of return on the initial investment, as a percentage?
items.s: Accounting rate of return = average profit/initial investment x 100 = 240000/1000000 x 100 = 24 percent.

items.q: A project is expected to bring in N1200000 in four years from now. The discount factor for year four is 0.683. What is the present value of that inflow?
items.s: Present value = cash flow x discount factor = 1200000 x 0.683 = 819600 naira.

items.q: A firm borrows at 10 percent and pays tax at 40 percent. What is the after tax cost of debt as a percentage?
items.s: After tax cost of debt = rate x (100 - tax)/100 = 10 x (100 - 40)/100 = 6 percent.

items.q: A company earned a profit after tax of N600000 and paid an ordinary dividend of N300000. What is the dividend payout ratio as a percentage?
items.s: Payout ratio = dividend/profit after tax x 100 = 300000/600000 x 100 = 50 percent.

items.q: Total cost was N110000 at an output of 2000 units and N230000 at an output of 10000 units. Using the high and low method, what is the fixed cost for the period?
A department has a fixed cost of N75000 for the period and a variable cost of N18 a unit. It produced 3000 units. What is the total cost?
items.s: Total cost = fixed + variable x units = 75000 + 18 x 3000 = 129000 naira.

items.q: Supervision costs N60000 for every 2000 units of output or part of that number. Material costs N12 a unit. What is the total of these two costs at an output of 8000 units?
items.s: The output needs 4 steps of supervision costing 4 x 60000 = 240000, so the total = 240000 + 12 x 8000 = 336000 naira.

items.q: Current assets are N750000, of which stock is N250000, and current liabilities are N250000. What is the acid test ratio, expressed as a whole number of times?
items.s: Acid test = (current assets - stock)/current liabilities = (750000 - 250000)/250000 = 2 times.

items.q: Operating profit for the year was N360000 and the capital employed was N5000000. What is the return on capital employed, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on capital employed = operating profit/capital employed x 100 = 360000/5000000 x 100 = 7.2 percent.

items.q: Trading profit before interest is N1200000 and the interest charge for the year is N200000. What is the interest cover, in times?
items.s: Interest cover = profit before interest/interest = 1200000/200000 = 6 times.

items.q: A firm has long term debt of N1500000 and shareholders' funds of N4200000. What is the gearing ratio, debt as a percentage of total long term funds?
items.s: Gearing = debt/(debt + equity) x 100 = 1500000/(1500000 + 4200000) x 100 = 26.32 percent.

items.q: Stock is held on average for 90 days, customers take 40 days to pay and the firm takes 25 days to pay its suppliers. What is the length of the cash operating cycle in days?
items.s: Cash cycle = stock days + receivable days - payable days = 90 + 40 - 25 = 105 days.

items.q: Annual demand for a material is 31250 units. The cost of placing one order is N100 and the cost of holding one unit for a year is N25. What is the economic order quantity in units?
items.s: Economic order quantity = square root of (2 x annual demand x order cost/holding cost) = square root of (2 x 31250 x 100/25) = square root of 250000 = 500 units.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 15000 units, opening finished stock is 1000 units and closing finished stock is 1800 units. What is the production budget?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 15000 + 1800 - 1000 = 15800 units.

items.q: The production budget is 5000 units. Each unit needs 3 hours at a wage rate of N100 an hour. What is the direct labour budget?
items.s: Labour budget = 5000 x 3 x 100 = 1500000 naira.

items.q: At a budgeted output of 4000 units the variable cost is N55 a unit and the fixed cost is N320000. What cost should be allowed if 5000 units are actually produced?
items.s: Allowed cost = 55 x 5000 + 320000 = 595000 naira.

items.q: The budget allowed spending of N900000 for the period and the actual spending was N950000. What is the variance, taking an underspend as positive and an overspend as negative?
items.s: Variance = allowed - actual = 900000 - 950000 = -50000 naira.

items.q: A product line sells for N1200000, its variable cost is N500000 and the fixed cost that would disappear if the line were dropped is N200000. What is the segment margin?
items.s: Segment margin = sales - variable cost - avoidable fixed cost = 1200000 - 500000 - 200000 = 500000 naira.

items.q: A product earns a contribution of N90 a unit and each unit needs 3 kilograms of a scarce material. What is the contribution per kilogram of the scarce material?
items.s: Contribution per kilogram = 90/3 = 30 naira.

items.q: A division earns a contribution of N240000 but carries fixed costs of N320000 that would be saved if it were closed. How much better off is the firm if the division is closed?
items.s: Closing saves fixed cost 320000 but loses contribution 240000, so the gain is 320000 - 240000 = 80000 naira.

items.q: A project costs N1200000 and brings in N300000 of cash a year for eight years. What is the payback period in years?
items.s: Payback = initial outlay/annual cash inflow = 1200000/300000 = 4 years.

items.q: A project costs N1000000 now and brings in N700000 after one year and N700000 after two years. The discount factors are 0.901 at year one and 0.797 at year two. What is the net present value?
A project costs N600000 and yields N220000 a year for 5 years with no discounting. What is the total surplus before any allowance for the cost of waiting?
items.s: Total inflow = 220000 x 5 = 1100000; surplus over cost = 1100000 - 600000 = 500000 naira.

items.q: A division earns a profit of N520000 on assets of N3200000, and the firm charges 12 percent for the funds employed. What is the residual income?
The full cost of a component is N110 and the transfer price is set at cost plus 10 percent. What is the transfer price?
items.s: Transfer price = 110 x (100 + 10)/100 = 121 naira.

items.q: A share currently sells for N200. The dividend just paid was N20 and dividends are expected to grow at 6 percent a year. Using the dividend growth model, what is the cost of equity as a percentage?
items.s: Next dividend = 20 x (100 + 6)/100 = 21.2; cost of equity = 21.2/200 x 100 + 6 = 16.6 percent.

items.q: A firm has equity of N4000000 costing 12 percent and debt of N3000000 costing 9 percent. Ignoring tax, what is the weighted average cost of capital as a percentage?
items.s: Weighted average = (4000000 x 12 + 3000000 x 9)/7000000 = 10.71 percent.

items.q: In the busiest month a firm made 12000 units at a total cost of N320000. In the quietest month it made 4000 units at a total cost of N160000. Using the high and low method, what is the variable cost per unit?
items.s: Variable cost per unit = change in cost/change in units = (320000 - 160000)/(12000 - 4000) = 20 naira.

items.s: Saving = purchase price - variable cost of making = 300000 - 260000 = 40000 naira; the fixed overhead does not change.

items.q: A customer offers to buy 2500 units at N45 each. The variable cost is N38 a unit and there is spare capacity, so no fixed cost changes. What extra contribution does the order bring?
items.s: Extra contribution = (price - variable cost) x units = (45 - 38) x 2500 = 17500 naira.

items.q: A machine costs N1200000 and is expected to earn an average annual profit of N300000 over its life. What is the accounting rate of return on the initial investment, as a percentage?
items.s: Accounting rate of return = average profit/initial investment x 100 = 300000/1200000 x 100 = 25 percent.

items.q: A project is expected to bring in N1200000 in four years from now. The discount factor for year four is 0.564. What is the present value of that inflow?
items.s: Present value = cash flow x discount factor = 1200000 x 0.564 = 676800 naira.

items.q: A division made a profit of N540000 on assets employed of N1600000. What return on investment did it earn, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on investment = 540000/1600000 x 100 = 33.75 percent.

items.q: A firm borrows at 8 percent and pays tax at 35 percent. What is the after tax cost of debt as a percentage?
items.s: After tax cost of debt = rate x (100 - tax)/100 = 8 x (100 - 35)/100 = 5.2 percent.

items.q: A company earned a profit after tax of N900000 and paid an ordinary dividend of N240000. What is the dividend payout ratio as a percentage?
items.s: Payout ratio = dividend/profit after tax x 100 = 240000/900000 x 100 = 26.67 percent.

A department has a fixed cost of N90000 for the period and a variable cost of N12 a unit. It produced 4000 units. What is the total cost?
items.s: Total cost = fixed + variable x units = 90000 + 12 x 4000 = 138000 naira.

items.q: Supervision costs N50000 for every 3000 units of output or part of that number. Material costs N10 a unit. What is the total of these two costs at an output of 8000 units?
items.s: The output needs 3 steps of supervision costing 3 x 50000 = 150000, so the total = 150000 + 10 x 8000 = 230000 naira.

items.q: Operating profit for the year was N480000 and the capital employed was N3000000. What is the return on capital employed, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on capital employed = operating profit/capital employed x 100 = 480000/3000000 x 100 = 16 percent.

items.q: Trading profit before interest is N1200000 and the interest charge for the year is N150000. What is the interest cover, in times?
items.s: Interest cover = profit before interest/interest = 1200000/150000 = 8 times.

items.q: A firm has long term debt of N1200000 and shareholders' funds of N3600000. What is the gearing ratio, debt as a percentage of total long term funds?
items.s: Gearing = debt/(debt + equity) x 100 = 1200000/(1200000 + 3600000) x 100 = 25 percent.

items.q: Sales for the year were N4800000 and total assets employed were N2400000. What is the asset turnover, in times?
items.s: Asset turnover = sales/total assets = 4800000/2400000 = 2 times.

items.q: Stock is held on average for 60 days, customers take 40 days to pay and the firm takes 20 days to pay its suppliers. What is the length of the cash operating cycle in days?
items.s: Cash cycle = stock days + receivable days - payable days = 60 + 40 - 20 = 80 days.

items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 12000 + 1200 - 1000 = 12200 units.

items.q: The production budget is 6000 units. Each unit needs 4 hours at a wage rate of N125 an hour. What is the direct labour budget?
items.s: Labour budget = 6000 x 4 x 125 = 3000000 naira.

items.q: A product earns a contribution of N90 a unit and each unit needs 2 kilograms of a scarce material. What is the contribution per kilogram of the scarce material?
items.s: Contribution per kilogram = 90/2 = 45 naira.

A project costs N600000 and yields N260000 a year for 4 years with no discounting. What is the total surplus before any allowance for the cost of waiting?
items.s: Total inflow = 260000 x 4 = 1040000; surplus over cost = 1040000 - 600000 = 440000 naira.

items.q: A division earns a profit of N400000 on assets of N2000000, and the firm charges 12 percent for the funds employed. What is the residual income?
A manager's unit has sales of N1000000, variable cost of N680000 and fixed cost under his control of N120000. What is the controllable margin?
items.s: Controllable margin = sales - variable cost - controllable fixed cost = 1000000 - 680000 - 120000 = 200000 naira.

items.q: A share currently sells for N240. The dividend just paid was N20 and dividends are expected to grow at 5 percent a year. Using the dividend growth model, what is the cost of equity as a percentage?
items.s: Next dividend = 20 x (100 + 5)/100 = 21; cost of equity = 21/240 x 100 + 5 = 13.75 percent.

items.q: The best definition of make or buy decision among these is

the choice between producing an item in house and obtaining it from outside
the resource in shortest supply that caps the level of activity
outlay that would cease if a particular activity were dropped

items.q: The statement “sales value less the cost of the materials used in the items sold” describes which of the following?

shut down decision
relevant cost
throughput contribution

items.q: The best definition of capital rationing among these is
o: the present worth of the returns divided by the sum first laid out
average yearly profit from a project shown as a percentage of the sum invested
a limit on the funds available for projects, so that the best must be chosen
the length of time taken for the money coming back to equal the sum first laid out
items.s: capital rationing: a limit on the funds available for projects, so that the best must be chosen. The other options describe accounting rate of return, profitability index, payback period.

items.q: transfer price is best described as

profit after a charge for the whole cost of the funds employed
the state in which what is best for a unit is also best for the whole firm
the amount one part of a firm charges another for goods or services
items.s: transfer price: the amount one part of a firm charges another for goods or services. The other options describe economic value added, goal congruence, balanced scorecard.

items.q: Which term is described by “the average number of days taken by customers to settle what they owe”?

economic order quantity
collection period
payment period
items.s: collection period is the average number of days taken by customers to settle what they owe.

items.q: Which term is described by “the money a project is worth today after allowing for the cost of waiting”?
o: profitability index
accounting rate of return
net present value
residual value
items.s: net present value is the money a project is worth today after allowing for the cost of waiting.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the state in which what is best for a unit is also best for the whole firm”
o: balanced scorecard
segment margin
goal congruence
controllable margin
items.s: goal congruence is the state in which what is best for a unit is also best for the whole firm.

items.q: sunk cost is best described as

the band of activity within which the assumed pattern of behaviour holds good
outlay that stays the same in total whatever the level of activity within the period
money spent already that no present choice can undo
items.s: sunk cost: money spent already that no present choice can undo. The other options describe relevant range, semi-variable cost, fixed cost.

items.q: The best definition of operating activities among these is
o: the part of the money summary that deals with buying and selling long lived assets
the rise or fall in the excess of current resources over short obligations
a short lived investment that can be turned into money at once with little risk
the part of the money summary that comes from the ordinary trading of the firm
items.s: operating activities: the part of the money summary that comes from the ordinary trading of the firm. The other options describe working capital movement, cash equivalent, investing activities.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what operating activities means.
o: an amount deducted from profit that involves no money leaving the firm
the rise or fall in the excess of current resources over short obligations
the part of the money summary that comes from the ordinary trading of the firm
the part of the money summary that deals with buying and selling long lived assets
items.s: operating activities: the part of the money summary that comes from the ordinary trading of the firm. The other options describe investing activities, working capital movement, non-cash charge.

items.q: In this course, shut down decision refers to
o: the choice whether to stop an activity whose contribution fails to cover its own fixed outlay
the resource in shortest supply that caps the level of activity
a future outlay that differs between the alternatives being weighed
sales value less the cost of the materials used in the items sold
items.s: shut down decision: the choice whether to stop an activity whose contribution fails to cover its own fixed outlay. The other options describe relevant cost, throughput contribution, limiting factor.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what gearing ratio means.
o: current resources without stock, divided by the obligations payable within a year
the resources held for the short term divided by the obligations payable within a year
sales value divided by the total resources used to earn it
the share of long term funds that carries a fixed return
items.s: gearing ratio: the share of long term funds that carries a fixed return. The other options describe acid test ratio, asset turnover, current ratio.

items.q: Which term is described by “the part of the money summary that deals with raising funds and paying them back”?
o: cash equivalent
financing activities

items.q: Supervision costs N50000 for every 2000 units of output or part of that number. Material costs N10 a unit. What is the total of these two costs at an output of 8000 units?
items.s: The output needs 4 steps of supervision costing 4 x 50000 = 200000, so the total = 200000 + 10 x 8000 = 280000 naira.

items.q: Operating profit for the year was N750000 and the capital employed was N5000000. What is the return on capital employed, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on capital employed = operating profit/capital employed x 100 = 750000/5000000 x 100 = 15 percent.

items.q: Trading profit before interest is N1800000 and the interest charge for the year is N300000. What is the interest cover, in times?
items.s: Interest cover = profit before interest/interest = 1800000/300000 = 6 times.

items.q: At a budgeted output of 4000 units the variable cost is N45 a unit and the fixed cost is N260000. What cost should be allowed if 6200 units are actually produced?
items.s: Allowed cost = 45 x 6200 + 260000 = 539000 naira.

items.q: A product line sells for N1500000, its variable cost is N500000 and the fixed cost that would disappear if the line were dropped is N200000. What is the segment margin?
items.s: Segment margin = sales - variable cost - avoidable fixed cost = 1500000 - 500000 - 200000 = 800000 naira.

items.q: A product earns a contribution of N120 a unit and each unit needs 5 kilograms of a scarce material. What is the contribution per kilogram of the scarce material?
items.s: Contribution per kilogram = 120/5 = 24 naira.

items.q: A project has a present value of future returns of N900000 and an initial cost of N500000. What is its profitability index?
items.s: Profitability index = present value of returns/initial cost = 900000/500000 = 1.8.

items.q: A division earns a profit of N640000 on assets of N2000000, and the firm charges 12 percent for the funds employed. What is the residual income?
A manager's unit has sales of N1200000, variable cost of N680000 and fixed cost under his control of N200000. What is the controllable margin?
items.s: Controllable margin = sales - variable cost - controllable fixed cost = 1200000 - 680000 - 200000 = 320000 naira.

items.q: A share currently sells for N240. The dividend just paid was N20 and dividends are expected to grow at 4 percent a year. Using the dividend growth model, what is the cost of equity as a percentage?
items.s: Next dividend = 20 x (100 + 4)/100 = 20.8; cost of equity = 20.8/240 x 100 + 4 = 12.67 percent.

items.q: In the busiest month a firm made 10000 units at a total cost of N210000. In the quietest month it made 2000 units at a total cost of N90000. Using the high and low method, what is the variable cost per unit?
items.s: Variable cost per unit = change in cost/change in units = (210000 - 90000)/(10000 - 2000) = 15 naira.

items.q: A department has a fixed cost of N90000 for the period and a variable cost of N12 a unit. It produced 3000 units. What is the total cost?
items.s: Total cost = fixed + variable x units = 90000 + 12 x 3000 = 126000 naira.

items.q: A firm has current assets of N1100000 and current liabilities of N260000. What is its working capital?
items.s: Working capital = current assets - current liabilities = 1100000 - 260000 = 840000 naira.

items.q: Sales for the year were N2000000 and the cost of the goods sold was N500000. What is the gross profit margin as a percentage of sales?
items.s: Gross margin = (sales - cost of sales)/sales x 100 = (2000000 - 500000)/2000000 x 100 = 75 percent.

items.q: Sales for the year were N3000000 and total assets employed were N1500000. What is the asset turnover, in times?
items.s: Asset turnover = sales/total assets = 3000000/1500000 = 2 times.

items.q: Cost of the goods sold for the year was N1500000 and the average stock held was N300000. How many times did stock turn over in the year?
items.s: Stock turnover = cost of goods sold/average stock = 1500000/300000 = 5 times.

items.q: Stock is held on average for 90 days, customers take 30 days to pay and the firm takes 20 days to pay its suppliers. What is the length of the cash operating cycle in days?
items.s: Cash cycle = stock days + receivable days - payable days = 90 + 30 - 20 = 100 days.

items.q: Annual demand for a material is 20000 units. The cost of placing one order is N80 and the cost of holding one unit for a year is N5. What is the economic order quantity in units?
items.s: Economic order quantity = square root of (2 x annual demand x order cost/holding cost) = square root of (2 x 20000 x 80/5) = square root of 640000 = 800 units.

items.q: The cash budget opens with a balance of N300000. Receipts are expected to be N1800000 and payments N1400000. What closing cash balance is budgeted?
items.s: Closing balance = opening + receipts - payments = 300000 + 1800000 - 1400000 = 700000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 12000 units, opening finished stock is 800 units and closing finished stock is 1800 units. What is the production budget?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 12000 + 1800 - 800 = 13000 units.

items.q: The production budget is 8000 units and each unit needs 4 kilograms of a material. Opening stock of the material is 2000 kilograms and closing stock is 1800 kilograms. What is the material purchase budget in kilograms?
The production budget is 6000 units. Each unit needs 2 hours at a wage rate of N100 an hour. What is the direct labour budget?
items.s: Labour budget = 6000 x 2 x 100 = 1200000 naira.

items.q: A part can be made in house for variable cost of N260000 or bought outside for N420000. Fixed overhead of N140000 is unaffected either way. What is the saving from making rather than buying?
items.s: Saving = purchase price - variable cost of making = 420000 - 260000 = 160000 naira; the fixed overhead does not change.

items.q: A customer offers to buy 2000 units at N50 each. The variable cost is N30 a unit and there is spare capacity, so no fixed cost changes. What extra contribution does the order bring?
items.s: Extra contribution = (price - variable cost) x units = (50 - 30) x 2000 = 40000 naira.

items.q: A machine costs N1000000 and is expected to earn an average annual profit of N300000 over its life. What is the accounting rate of return on the initial investment, as a percentage?
items.s: Accounting rate of return = average profit/initial investment x 100 = 300000/1000000 x 100 = 30 percent.

items.s: Present value = cash flow x discount factor = 800000 x 0.683 = 546400 naira.

items.q: A division made a profit of N420000 on assets employed of N2100000. What return on investment did it earn, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on investment = 420000/2100000 x 100 = 20 percent.

items.q: A firm has equity of N3000000 costing 18 percent and debt of N2000000 costing 8 percent. Ignoring tax, what is the weighted average cost of capital as a percentage?
items.s: Weighted average = (3000000 x 18 + 2000000 x 8)/5000000 = 14 percent.

items.q: A firm borrows at 10 percent and pays tax at 30 percent. What is the after tax cost of debt as a percentage?
items.s: After tax cost of debt = rate x (100 - tax)/100 = 10 x (100 - 30)/100 = 7 percent.

items.q: A company earned a profit after tax of N720000 and paid an ordinary dividend of N300000. What is the dividend payout ratio as a percentage?
items.s: Payout ratio = dividend/profit after tax x 100 = 300000/720000 x 100 = 41.67 percent.

items.q: A product earns a contribution of N120 a unit and each unit needs 3 kilograms of a scarce material. What is the contribution per kilogram of the scarce material?
items.s: Contribution per kilogram = 120/3 = 40 naira.

items.q: A division earns a profit of N400000 on assets of N2000000, and the firm charges 8 percent for the funds employed. What is the residual income?
A manager's unit has sales of N1000000, variable cost of N680000 and fixed cost under his control of N160000. What is the controllable margin?
items.s: Controllable margin = sales - variable cost - controllable fixed cost = 1000000 - 680000 - 160000 = 160000 naira.

items.q: A share currently sells for N200. The dividend just paid was N20 and dividends are expected to grow at 4 percent a year. Using the dividend growth model, what is the cost of equity as a percentage?
items.s: Next dividend = 20 x (100 + 4)/100 = 20.8; cost of equity = 20.8/200 x 100 + 4 = 14.4 percent.

items.q: In the busiest month a firm made 12000 units at a total cost of N400000. In the quietest month it made 3000 units at a total cost of N130000. Using the high and low method, what is the variable cost per unit?
items.s: Variable cost per unit = change in cost/change in units = (400000 - 130000)/(12000 - 3000) = 30 naira.

items.q: A department has a fixed cost of N75000 for the period and a variable cost of N24 a unit. It produced 3000 units. What is the total cost?
items.s: Total cost = fixed + variable x units = 75000 + 24 x 3000 = 147000 naira.

items.q: A firm has current assets of N600000 and current liabilities of N300000. What is the current ratio, expressed as a whole number of times?
items.s: Current ratio = current assets/current liabilities = 600000/300000 = 2 times.

items.q: A firm has current assets of N780000 and current liabilities of N260000. What is its working capital?
items.s: Working capital = current assets - current liabilities = 780000 - 260000 = 520000 naira.

items.q: Sales for the year were N2400000 and total assets employed were N2400000. What is the asset turnover, in times?
items.s: Asset turnover = sales/total assets = 2400000/2400000 = 1 times.

items.q: Stock is held on average for 90 days, customers take 30 days to pay and the firm takes 35 days to pay its suppliers. What is the length of the cash operating cycle in days?
items.s: Cash cycle = stock days + receivable days - payable days = 90 + 30 - 35 = 85 days.

items.q: Annual demand for a material is 16000 units. The cost of placing one order is N80 and the cost of holding one unit for a year is N4. What is the economic order quantity in units?
items.s: Economic order quantity = square root of (2 x annual demand x order cost/holding cost) = square root of (2 x 16000 x 80/4) = square root of 640000 = 800 units.

items.q: The cash budget opens with a balance of N180000. Receipts are expected to be N2100000 and payments N1400000. What closing cash balance is budgeted?
items.s: Closing balance = opening + receipts - payments = 180000 + 2100000 - 1400000 = 880000 naira.

items.q: Budgeted sales are 9000 units, opening finished stock is 1500 units and closing finished stock is 2000 units. What is the production budget?
items.s: Production = sales + closing stock - opening stock = 9000 + 2000 - 1500 = 9500 units.

items.q: The production budget is 6000 units and each unit needs 2 kilograms of a material. Opening stock of the material is 2000 kilograms and closing stock is 2500 kilograms. What is the material purchase budget in kilograms?
The production budget is 6000 units. Each unit needs 2 hours at a wage rate of N150 an hour. What is the direct labour budget?
items.s: Labour budget = 6000 x 2 x 150 = 1800000 naira.

items.q: A part can be made in house for variable cost of N220000 or bought outside for N360000. Fixed overhead of N140000 is unaffected either way. What is the saving from making rather than buying?
items.s: Saving = purchase price - variable cost of making = 360000 - 220000 = 140000 naira; the fixed overhead does not change.

items.q: A customer offers to buy 2500 units at N50 each. The variable cost is N34 a unit and there is spare capacity, so no fixed cost changes. What extra contribution does the order bring?
items.s: Extra contribution = (price - variable cost) x units = (50 - 34) x 2500 = 40000 naira.

items.q: A project costs N1500000 and brings in N300000 of cash a year for eight years. What is the payback period in years?
items.s: Payback = initial outlay/annual cash inflow = 1500000/300000 = 5 years.

items.q: A machine costs N1500000 and is expected to earn an average annual profit of N300000 over its life. What is the accounting rate of return on the initial investment, as a percentage?
items.s: Accounting rate of return = average profit/initial investment x 100 = 300000/1500000 x 100 = 20 percent.

items.q: A project costs N600000 and yields N260000 a year for 5 years with no discounting. What is the total surplus before any allowance for the cost of waiting?
items.s: Total inflow = 260000 x 5 = 1300000; surplus over cost = 1300000 - 600000 = 700000 naira.

items.q: A division made a profit of N540000 on assets employed of N2100000. What return on investment did it earn, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on investment = 540000/2100000 x 100 = 25.71 percent.

items.q: The full cost of a component is N160 and the transfer price is set at cost plus 20 percent. What is the transfer price?
items.s: Transfer price = 160 x (100 + 20)/100 = 192 naira.

valuing a share from the payout just made, its expected rise and the return required
the return that holders of ordinary shares expect on their stake
the effective rate a firm pays on borrowed money once tax relief is allowed for

the number of times trading profit can meet the yearly charge on borrowed money
the resources held for the short term divided by the obligations payable within a year
current resources without stock, divided by the obligations payable within a year

items.q: Stock is held on average for 60 days, customers take 30 days to pay and the firm takes 20 days to pay its suppliers. What is the length of the cash operating cycle in days?

items.q: Annual demand for a material is 10000 units. The cost of placing one order is N125 and the cost of holding one unit for a year is N10. What is the economic order quantity in units?

items.q: Each unit of a product needs 2 machine hours, the contribution is N30 a unit and fixed costs are N60000. Only 6000 machine hours are available. What is the highest profit obtainable?
items.s: Units possible = 6000/2 = 3000; contribution = 3000 x 30 = 90000; profit = 90000 - 60000 = 30000 naira.

items.q: A project costs N1500000 now and brings in N800000 after one year and N700000 after two years. The discount factors are 0.901 at year one and 0.826 at year two. What is the net present value?

items.q: In the busiest month a firm made 10000 units at a total cost of N280000. In the quietest month it made 5000 units at a total cost of N180000. Using the high and low method, what is the variable cost per unit?
items.s: Variable cost per unit = change in cost/change in units = (280000 - 180000)/(10000 - 5000) = 20 naira.

items.q: Total cost was N160000 at an output of 2000 units and N340000 at an output of 8000 units. Using the high and low method, what is the fixed cost for the period?

items.q: Current assets are N600000, of which stock is N200000, and current liabilities are N200000. What is the acid test ratio, expressed as a whole number of times?

items.q: Cost of the goods sold for the year was N1200000 and the average stock held was N300000. How many times did stock turn over in the year?
items.s: Stock turnover = cost of goods sold/average stock = 1200000/300000 = 4 times.

items.q: The cash budget opens with a balance of N240000. Receipts are expected to be N1800000 and payments N1950000. What closing cash balance is budgeted?

items.q: The production budget is 6000 units and each unit needs 4 kilograms of a material. Opening stock of the material is 1000 kilograms and closing stock is 2500 kilograms. What is the material purchase budget in kilograms?

items.q: The budget allowed spending of N600000 for the period and the actual spending was N860000. What is the variance, taking an underspend as positive and an overspend as negative?

items.q: A part can be made in house for variable cost of N220000 or bought outside for N360000. Fixed overhead of N110000 is unaffected either way. What is the saving from making rather than buying?
