items.q: A product line sells for N1500000, its variable cost is N500000 and the fixed cost that would disappear if the line were dropped is N150000. What is the segment margin?
items.s: Segment margin = sales - variable cost - avoidable fixed cost = 1500000 - 500000 - 150000 = 850000 naira.

items.q: A machine costs N800000 and is expected to earn an average annual profit of N240000 over its life. What is the accounting rate of return on the initial investment, as a percentage?
items.s: Accounting rate of return = average profit/initial investment x 100 = 240000/800000 x 100 = 30 percent.

items.q: A project costs N800000 and yields N300000 a year for 4 years with no discounting. What is the total surplus before any allowance for the cost of waiting?
items.s: Total inflow = 300000 x 4 = 1200000; surplus over cost = 1200000 - 800000 = 400000 naira.

items.q: A division earns a profit of N400000 on assets of N3200000, and the firm charges 8 percent for the funds employed. What is the residual income?
A division made a profit of N420000 on assets employed of N1600000. What return on investment did it earn, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on investment = 420000/1600000 x 100 = 26.25 percent.

items.q: The full cost of a component is N90 and the transfer price is set at cost plus 10 percent. What is the transfer price?
items.s: Transfer price = 90 x (100 + 10)/100 = 99 naira.

items.q: A manager's unit has sales of N1000000, variable cost of N420000 and fixed cost under his control of N160000. What is the controllable margin?
items.s: Controllable margin = sales - variable cost - controllable fixed cost = 1000000 - 420000 - 160000 = 420000 naira.

items.q: A share currently sells for N200. The dividend just paid was N24 and dividends are expected to grow at 5 percent a year. Using the dividend growth model, what is the cost of equity as a percentage?
items.s: Next dividend = 24 x (100 + 5)/100 = 25.2; cost of equity = 25.2/200 x 100 + 5 = 17.6 percent.

items.q: A company earned a profit after tax of N720000 and paid an ordinary dividend of N240000. What is the dividend payout ratio as a percentage?
items.s: Payout ratio = dividend/profit after tax x 100 = 240000/720000 x 100 = 33.33 percent.

items.q: Sales for the year were N3600000 and total assets employed were N1800000. What is the asset turnover, in times?
items.s: Asset turnover = sales/total assets = 3600000/1800000 = 2 times.

items.q: Stock is held on average for 45 days, customers take 40 days to pay and the firm takes 35 days to pay its suppliers. What is the length of the cash operating cycle in days?

A firm has equity of N4000000 costing 12 percent and debt of N4000000 costing 8 percent. Ignoring tax, what is the weighted average cost of capital as a percentage?

items.s: The output needs 2 steps of supervision costing 2 x 50000 = 100000, so the total = 100000 + 15 x 5000 = 175000 naira.

items.q: Sales for the year were N800000 and the cost of the goods sold was N500000. What is the gross profit margin as a percentage of sales?
items.s: Gross margin = (sales - cost of sales)/sales x 100 = (800000 - 500000)/800000 x 100 = 37.5 percent.

items.q: Operating profit for the year was N600000 and the capital employed was N3000000. What is the return on capital employed, as a percentage?
items.s: Return on capital employed = operating profit/capital employed x 100 = 600000/3000000 x 100 = 20 percent.

items.q: Trading profit before interest is N900000 and the interest charge for the year is N150000. What is the interest cover, in times?
items.s: Interest cover = profit before interest/interest = 900000/150000 = 6 times.

items.q: Cost of the goods sold for the year was N1200000 and the average stock held was N200000. How many times did stock turn over in the year?
items.s: Stock turnover = cost of goods sold/average stock = 1200000/200000 = 6 times.

a one-off request to supply at a price below the normal one
outlay that would cease if a particular activity were dropped
the resource in shortest supply that caps the level of activity

items.q: balanced scorecard may be defined as

profit left after deducting a charge for the resources a unit employs
the amount one part of a firm charges another for goods or services
what a manager earns on the items his own decisions can change

o: master budget
budget
cash budget
incremental budgeting

accounting rate of return
profitability index
discount factor

the return the suppliers of funds must be offered to part with their money
the extra danger to shareholders that arises from borrowing

outlay that the manager of a unit is able to influence by his own decisions

an amount deducted from profit that involves no money leaving the firm
the part of the money summary that comes from the ordinary trading of the firm
items.s: investing activities: the part of the money summary that deals with buying and selling long lived assets. The other options describe non-cash charge, operating activities, cash flow statement.

items.q: In this course, budget slack refers to
o: a forecast of money coming in, money going out and the balance left
the set of linked plans that together form the whole forecast for a period
the cushion a manager builds into his plan to make the target easier to beat
building every figure afresh so each item must be justified from nothing
items.s: budget slack: the cushion a manager builds into his plan to make the target easier to beat. The other options describe master budget, cash budget, zero-based budgeting.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines asset turnover?
o: the study of relationships between figures in the accounts to judge how a firm is doing
the share of long term funds that carries a fixed return
a measure of whether a firm can meet the obligations falling due shortly
sales value divided by the total resources used to earn it
items.s: asset turnover: sales value divided by the total resources used to earn it. The other options describe ratio analysis, liquidity ratio, gearing ratio.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the part of the profit of the year handed to the ordinary shareholders”
o: cost of debt
weighted average cost of capital
dividend payout ratio
cost of capital
items.s: dividend payout ratio is the part of the profit of the year handed to the ordinary shareholders.

items.q: payment period may be defined as
o: the excess of current resources over the obligations falling due within a year
the number of times the average holding is sold in the course of a year
the average number of days the firm takes to settle what it owes suppliers
the batch size at which the cost of ordering and the cost of holding stock are lowest together
items.s: payment period: the average number of days the firm takes to settle what it owes suppliers. The other options describe working capital, inventory turnover, economic order quantity.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the extra danger to shareholders that arises from borrowing”
o: dividend payout ratio
retained earnings
financial risk
cost of equity
items.s: financial risk is the extra danger to shareholders that arises from borrowing.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines variable cost?
o: outlay that moves in direct proportion to the number of items produced
money spent already that no present choice can undo
the worth of the best choice given up in order to take another
the band of activity within which the assumed pattern of behaviour holds good
items.s: variable cost: outlay that moves in direct proportion to the number of items produced. The other options describe opportunity cost, relevant range, sunk cost.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains cash equivalent.
o: the rise or fall in the excess of current resources over short obligations
a summary of the money that moved in and out of the firm during a period
the part of the money summary that comes from the ordinary trading of the firm
a short lived investment that can be turned into money at once with little risk
items.s: cash equivalent: a short lived investment that can be turned into money at once with little risk. The other options describe operating activities, working capital movement, cash flow statement.

items.q: “average yearly profit from a project shown as a percentage of the sum invested” is the definition of
o: net present value
payback period
accounting rate of return
discount factor
items.s: accounting rate of return is average yearly profit from a project shown as a percentage of the sum invested.

items.q: The correct meaning of interest cover is
o: the resources held for the short term divided by the obligations payable within a year
current resources without stock, divided by the obligations payable within a year
the number of times trading profit can meet the yearly charge on borrowed money
sales value divided by the total resources used to earn it
items.s: interest cover: the number of times trading profit can meet the yearly charge on borrowed money. The other options describe asset turnover, current ratio, acid test ratio.

items.q: In this course, opportunity cost refers to
o: outlay that stays the same in total whatever the level of activity within the period
working out the variable part per unit from the difference between the busiest and quietest periods
money spent already that no present choice can undo
the worth of the best choice given up in order to take another
items.s: opportunity cost: the worth of the best choice given up in order to take another. The other options describe fixed cost, sunk cost, high and low method.

items.q: The correct meaning of make or buy decision is
o: a one-off request to supply at a price below the normal one
outlay that would cease if a particular activity were dropped
the choice whether to stop an activity whose contribution fails to cover its own fixed outlay
the choice between producing an item in house and obtaining it from outside
items.s: make or buy decision: the choice between producing an item in house and obtaining it from outside. The other options describe avoidable cost, special order, shut down decision.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines inventory turnover?
o: a position in which a firm grows faster than the funds it has to support the growth
the stretch of time from paying for stock to collecting the cash from its sale
the number of times the average holding is sold in the course of a year
a reduction allowed for settling an amount before the date it falls due
items.s: inventory turnover: the number of times the average holding is sold in the course of a year. The other options describe overtrading, cash discount, operating cycle.

items.q: “the stretch of time from paying for stock to collecting the cash from its sale” is the definition of
o: collection period
working capital
operating cycle
inventory turnover
items.s: operating cycle is the stretch of time from paying for stock to collecting the cash from its sale.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a future outlay that differs between the alternatives being weighed”
o: relevant cost
limiting factor
special order
unavoidable cost
items.s: relevant cost is a future outlay that differs between the alternatives being weighed.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains incremental budgeting.
o: a plan kept the same length by adding a further period each time one expires
a forecast of money coming in, money going out and the balance left
building next period on the figures of this one with a margin added
a quantified plan covering a stated stretch of time
items.s: incremental budgeting: building next period on the figures of this one with a margin added. The other options describe rolling budget, cash budget, budget.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines discount factor?
o: the amount by which a future sum is scaled down to state it in today's terms
what a project or asset is expected to fetch at the close of its useful life
the present worth of the returns divided by the sum first laid out
the discount percentage at which a project is worth exactly nothing today
items.s: discount factor: the amount by which a future sum is scaled down to state it in today's terms. The other options describe residual value, internal rate of return, profitability index.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains management by exception.
o: a part of the firm in which outlay is gathered without any measure of output being attached
the practice of acting only on the differences that are large enough to matter
a part of the firm answerable for both its revenue and its spending
a part of the firm answerable for profit and also for the assets it employs
items.s: management by exception: the practice of acting only on the differences that are large enough to matter. The other options describe cost centre, investment centre, profit centre.
items.t: Nature and scope of management accounting

items.q: “the batch size at which the cost of ordering and the cost of holding stock are lowest together” is the definition of
o: collection period
economic order quantity
working capital
inventory turnover
items.s: economic order quantity is the batch size at which the cost of ordering and the cost of holding stock are lowest together.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains cash discount.
o: a position in which a firm grows faster than the funds it has to support the growth
the batch size at which the cost of ordering and the cost of holding stock are lowest together
the excess of current resources over the obligations falling due within a year
a reduction allowed for settling an amount before the date it falls due
items.s: cash discount: a reduction allowed for settling an amount before the date it falls due. The other options describe working capital, overtrading, economic order quantity.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the practice of acting only on the differences that are large enough to matter”
o: investment centre
controllable cost
cost centre
management by exception
items.s: management by exception is the practice of acting only on the differences that are large enough to matter.
items.t: Nature and scope of management accounting

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains controllable cost.
o: a part of the firm answerable for both its revenue and its spending
outlay that the manager of a unit is able to influence by his own decisions
a part of the firm in which outlay is gathered without any measure of output being attached
the practice of acting only on the differences that are large enough to matter
items.s: controllable cost: outlay that the manager of a unit is able to influence by his own decisions. The other options describe profit centre, cost centre, management by exception.
items.t: Nature and scope of management accounting

items.q: The correct meaning of flexible budget is
o: a forecast of money coming in, money going out and the balance left
a quantified plan covering a stated stretch of time
a plan redrawn at the level of activity that was actually reached
building every figure afresh so each item must be justified from nothing
items.s: flexible budget: a plan redrawn at the level of activity that was actually reached. The other options describe zero-based budgeting, cash budget, budget.

items.q: “the set of linked plans that together form the whole forecast for a period” is the definition of
o: master budget
cash budget
incremental budgeting
budget slack
items.s: master budget is the set of linked plans that together form the whole forecast for a period.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a part of the firm answerable for both its revenue and its spending”
o: cost centre
profit centre
controllable cost
management accounting
items.s: profit centre is a part of the firm answerable for both its revenue and its spending.
items.t: Nature and scope of management accounting

items.q: The correct meaning of economic value added is
o: profit after a charge for the whole cost of the funds employed
a set of measures covering money, customers, internal work and learning
what a part of the business earns after its own avoidable outlay is charged
the surplus a unit of the firm makes after charging the items it controls
items.s: economic value added: profit after a charge for the whole cost of the funds employed. The other options describe balanced scorecard, divisional profit, segment margin.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines financial accounting?
o: the branch that reports the results of a firm to parties outside it
a part of the firm in which outlay is gathered without any measure of output being attached
the practice of acting only on the differences that are large enough to matter
a part of the firm answerable for profit and also for the assets it employs
items.s: financial accounting: the branch that reports the results of a firm to parties outside it. The other options describe investment centre, management by exception, cost centre.
items.t: Nature and scope of management accounting

items.q: In this course, controllable cost refers to
o: a part of the firm in which outlay is gathered without any measure of output being attached
a part of the firm answerable for both its revenue and its spending
outlay that the manager of a unit is able to influence by his own decisions
a part of the firm answerable for profit and also for the assets it employs
items.s: controllable cost: outlay that the manager of a unit is able to influence by his own decisions. The other options describe profit centre, cost centre, investment centre.
items.t: Nature and scope of management accounting

items.q: In this course, dividend growth model refers to
o: the effective rate a firm pays on borrowed money once tax relief is allowed for
valuing a share from the payout just made, its expected rise and the return required
the extra danger to shareholders that arises from borrowing
the return that holders of ordinary shares expect on their stake
items.s: dividend growth model: valuing a share from the payout just made, its expected rise and the return required. The other options describe cost of equity, financial risk, cost of debt.

items.q: The correct meaning of special order is
o: the choice between producing an item in house and obtaining it from outside
the choice whether to stop an activity whose contribution fails to cover its own fixed outlay
a one-off request to supply at a price below the normal one
outlay that carries on whether or not a particular activity continues
items.s: special order: a one-off request to supply at a price below the normal one. The other options describe shut down decision, unavoidable cost, make or buy decision.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines working capital?
o: the number of times the average holding is sold in the course of a year
the average number of days taken by customers to settle what they owe
the excess of current resources over the obligations falling due within a year
the average number of days the firm takes to settle what it owes suppliers
items.s: working capital: the excess of current resources over the obligations falling due within a year. The other options describe collection period, payment period, inventory turnover.
